text:
incident-bot: Incident created: high-rate CUDA OOMs on serving-runtime-prod (model=redwood-7b, region=us-west-2) :rotating_light:

alice.nguyen: seeing a spike in OOMs starting ~3309998700, nodes flapping (killed container + node reboot) — error budget alert fired.

ben.santos: +1, graphs show token error rate up from 0.2% -> 6% in the last 10m. Latency also up. Pinning to a few nodes: gpu-node-09, gpu-node-11, gpu-node-14.

carla.ops: stacktrace from runtime on gpu-node-11: ```
E CUDA: out of memory when allocating 2.3 GiB (attempt to reserve)
allocator: reserved_blocks=512 free_blocks=23 fragmented=0.73
KV cache prefetch: queued=18 inflight=4
```

alice.nguyen: weird — headroom reported ~12GB available on those nodes via telemetry, but allocator shows fragmented free. Suspect reserved-block fragmentation + aggressive prefetch.

ben.santos: I can confirm telemetry headroom metric (node-level) comes from cgroup limit minus used. It doesn't account for reserved block fragmentation in the allocator. So headroom != usable contiguous chunk.

dave.ml: repro hypothesis: continuous prefetch of KV cache creates many small reserved blocks, causing fragmentation. When a large allocation needed for generation, allocate fails despite headroom.

carla.ops: customers affected: 3 large Dedicated tenants on us-west-2 saw elevated 5xx from their serving endpoints. We're seeing 503 rate up ~4%.

alice.nguyen: immediate mitigation idea: 1) disable KV prefetch on affected node pool, 2) drain/evict and restart pods on the three nodes to defragment allocator, 3) temporarily increase reserve/shrink threshold so allocator coalesces.

ben.santos: agreed. I'll disable prefetch via runtime flag for the node group: ```/api/admin/runtime/config -d '{"kv_prefetch_enabled": false}'```

carla.ops: doing graceful drain on gpu-node-11 now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PD-INC-7234 (oncall=carla.ops).

carla.ops: restarting runtime on gpu-node-09 and gpu-node-14 as well. Restart command: `systemctl restart redwood-runtime` (rolling, 30s gap).

ben.santos: applied config to disable prefetch across pool. Confirmed flag rolled out to 4/4 runtime instances.

alice.nguyen: telemetry after disabling prefetch: KV prefetch queue dropped to 0 in ~40s. Memory allocation failures still occurring on one pod (on gpu-node-14) — possibly needs full restart to free reserved blocks.

dave.ml: recommendation: trigger admin API to evict and rebuild allocator arena on restart. We have an endpoint: `POST /internal/allocator/rebuild` — run after container restart to ensure arenas compact.

carla.ops: performed node restarts and called allocator rebuild on restarted pods. Logs now show `allocator: rebuild complete, contiguous_free=11GB` on gpu-node-11.

ben.santos: service error rate dropping back to baseline. Still keeping an eye. Rolling back will be to re-enable prefetch cautiously.

alice.nguyen: customer impact note: affected customers received ~2-3m of elevated 5xx and a small backlog; no data loss, requests retried by client. Notified CSMs to expect brief complaints.

dave.ml: root cause hypothesis: over-aggressive KV prefetch combined with small reserved-block slab sizes caused fragmentation; headroom metric reported at node-level doesn't reflect allocator fragmentation or reserved-block internal slack.

carla.ops: follow-ups: 
- open runtime ticket to expose allocator contiguous-free metric to telemetry (action: ben.santos)
- add guardrail to disable prefetch when contiguous_free < X GB (action: dave.ml)
- improve headroom calc or add fragmentation correction (action: eng-runtime)

ben.santos: opened ENG-4567 (allocator-visible-contiguous-metric) and assigned to eng-runtime.

alice.nguyen: pausing re-enable of prefetch. We'll run a small canary with controlled prefetch window once contiguous-free telemetry is available.

carla.ops: handing off to night oncall @ben.santos for monitoring. Summary for handoff: 
- incident created at 3309998888, primary mitigations applied: KV prefetch disabled, affected pods restarted, allocator rebuilt on restarted pods.
- current status: error rate normalized, nodes stable.
- customer impact: short 2-3m elevated 5xx for 3 Dedicated tenants in us-west-2. CSMs notified.
- follow-ups: ENG-4567, guardrail ticket ENG-4568, add runbook step to evacuate if contiguous_free < threshold.

ben.santos: taking handoff. I'll keep 15m watch, escalate if anything resurfaces. Marking incident as mitigated in incident tracker and updating PD incident.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-INC-7234 status changed to "Mitigated" by ben.santos.

alice.nguyen: one last note — add a log-level metric for `allocator: failed_allocs_contiguous_needed` to correlate with headroom. Helps avoid false headroom confidence. (asked eng-runtime)

carla.ops: thanks all. Closing thread after handoff if stable. :white_check_mark:

ben.santos: will file short postmortem draft and include timelines, customer impact, and recommended next steps.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated): mitigation window 10m, monitor 1h."
